about.lead: Malls, banks, and HR teams — most of what I've built lives behind a login screen. Three years in, the interesting part is rarely the framework. It's working out how a business actually runs, then making the software agree with it.
about.body: I came in through the data side — schemas, ERP flows, migrations — which is why I still design the database before I design the screen. Then AI got its hooks in me. Now a good chunk of my work is CV screening, OCR pipelines, and the parts of a workflow nobody should be doing by hand.

principles.title: Model the data first
principles.body: Schemas outlive interfaces. Get the relationships right and features stop fighting each other six months in.

principles.title: Ship it, then polish
principles.body: A staging environment nobody uses proves nothing. Put it in front of real users early and let their habits shape the next iteration.

principles.title: Automate the tedious parts
principles.body: Screening, OCR, reporting — if someone is copy-pasting between tabs, that's a feature waiting to be built.

education.label: Education
education.story: Information Systems turned out to be the right accident. I spent those years tracing how data moves through a company — schemas, ERP flows, the messy handoffs nobody documents — and somewhere in the middle of it, fell for AI.
